citation: Huh D.-A., Huh E.-H., Byeon S.-H., Sohn J.-R., Moon K. W. (2019) Development of Accident Probability Index Using Surrogate Indicators of Chemical Accidents in Chemical Plants. IJERPH 16(18), 3271. doi:10.3390/ijerph16183271

dedupe_keys.name: accident probability index for screening chemical plants from surrogate indicators south korea 2019

description: The accident probability index estimates how likely a chemical plant is to have an accident from four readily available surrogate indicators, so that regulators can screen high-risk plants without the confidential process data that full risk indices need. The indicators, chosen from a literature survey and interviews with chemical experts and government chemical managers, are the hazard characteristics of the chemicals, the volume handled, the plant's own accident record and the national accident frequency of each chemical. Applied to 4,520 chemical plants, the index averaged 5.324, each 10-point increase raised the odds of an actual accident 1.06 times, and plants in the top quartile had 4.30 times the accident frequency of those in the bottom quartile. It was developed by Da-An Huh and co-authors and published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health on 5 September 2019. Coverage is South Korea. The article is available free online under CC BY 4.0; the plant data are not released. Caveats: the index uses national data and weights tied to Korean regulation, and it screens plants, not predicting specific scenarios. For simulation it gives a simple way to assign relative accident likelihoods to many chemical plants in hazard exposure and domino effect studies. It is related to the Ulsan chlorine leak selective evacuation case study record in this catalogue.
